meta.name: Forge Builder corpus
meta.note: Every boundary citation is a real file:line in that checkout, not a paraphrase. The Builder consumes this corpus BEFORE touching code so its first pass is grounded; the sandbox wiring + '5 clean diffs in a row' exit criterion of brief step 2 remain a separate phase.

patterns.name: adopt-before-load
patterns.trigger: claim orphaned records, missing owner, user_id undefined, pre-login capture, adopt orphans, session boundary healing
recipe: At the REAL auth boundary (a session just resolved), find every local record with no owner key.
Stamp the authenticated owner + mark the row unsynced so it re-enters the sync path.
Re-stamp any queued payloads for the same local ids so a pending flush does not dead-letter again.
Run BEFORE the tenant-scoped load so the claimed rows are visible to their new owner.
acceptance: records previously invisible to tenant reads become visible and syncable
ownership is NEVER rewritten for a record that already carries any user_id
no session => early return, zero writes
patterns.guardrail: Fail closed and idempotent: an orphan is claimed exactly once; adoption never rewrites ownership away from another user. A failure is captured and logged, never silent.

patterns.name: gate-the-shell-on-a-real-session
patterns.trigger: signup no session, email confirmation pending, guard mount, session gate, null session, confirm email state
recipe: Treat a successful SIGNUP without a returned session as UNRESOLVED, not success (email confirmation is pending).
Enter the shell only when a real session object exists; otherwise render an explicit confirm-your-email state with a resend action.
acceptance: shell state derives from (!!session), never from the absence of an error
confirm-pending branch exists and offers resend with i18n coverage
patterns.guardrail: Fail closed: a null session never mounts tenant state, so records can never again be created under user_id undefined.

patterns.name: realtime-live-update
patterns.trigger: multi device live sync, postgres_changes, realtime delivery, subscription not delivered, realtime publication, live update ui
recipe: Add an idempotent migration: alter publication supabase_realtime add table ... for each table you need live.
Subscribe to postgres_changes on the user's OWN rows only, with filter user_id=eq.<userId>; RLS additionally scopes the stream.
On each delta, apply it to the local store idempotently, then reload tenant state so the open UI updates without a manual pull or reload.
Remember: a channel reaching SUBSCRIBED does NOT prove delivery — publication membership is the actual gate.
acceptance: live two-device simulation proves the event is DELIVERED (scripted probe), not merely subscribed
foreign rows never merge into the user's ledger
patterns.guardrail: Fail closed: client-side ownership assertion is a second line of defense on top of RLS. Cleanup removes the channel on unmount/offline.

patterns.name: idempotent-local-apply-with-status
patterns.trigger: apply remote change, upsert local, foreign row ignore, return code 0 1 2, idempotent application, delta apply observability
recipe: Shape the apply as a pure function returning a typed integer status: 0 applied, 1 ignored (foreign/absent), 2 failure.
Upsert/delete by the LOCAL stable id (local_id), never by server-only id.
Map every failure to a capture/error record; never throw into the render path.
acceptance: tests assert all three return codes including the foreign-row ignore path
a repeated delta is a no-op-by-upsert (idempotent)
patterns.guardrail: No silent drops and no silent merges: a stranger's row is recorded as ignored, a failure is captured with context.

patterns.name: single-shared-tenant-loader
patterns.trigger: tenant load, duplicate resolution logic, two paths same state, loadTenantState, logic drift, shared loader
recipe: When two code paths must resolve the same tenant state (initial session load AND live-update reload), extract ONE loader both call.
The loader resolves businesses, transactions, the active business, and the per-user preference in one place.
acceptance: initial load and realtime reload produce identical resolution for the same user
no second copy of the resolution logic exists
patterns.guardrail: Single source of truth: the same function is what both the realtime hook and the session effect execute, so behavior cannot drift.

patterns.name: fail-closed-telemetry
patterns.trigger: telemetry, analytics consent, opt in, share usage stats, privacy toggle, no network without consent, flush gate
recipe: Hold consent in the app store as a boolean defaulting to false (OFF).
track() only writes the local log when consent is off — no buffering of non-opted-in telemetry.
flush() REFUSES to hit the network without consent and purges any un-consented backlog.
Surface the toggle in Settings with an on-device privacy statement.
acceptance: no network call is ever attempted while consent is off
a flush requested before consent purges the backlog instead of sending
the toggle reflects the store default of false
patterns.guardrail: Fail closed: OFF by default; consent is required before ANY event leaves the device; a silent network attempt is a bug, not a default.

patterns.name: unconfigured-builds-fail-closed
patterns.trigger: vapid missing, external config absent, unconfigured status, capability status, broken prompt, push reminders disabled
recipe: A capability requiring external config (e.g. VAPID key) must report its build state: absent config => 'unconfigured'.
The Settings UI renders that status to the user instead of invoking a broken subscription flow or a missing-key error.
acceptance: status returns 'unconfigured' when the key is absent
the UI shows the state rather than a dead control
patterns.guardrail: Fail closed: absence of configuration is surfaced as a status, never as a silent no-op or a thrown error the user cannot read.

patterns.name: version-truth
patterns.trigger: app version, stale version, version string, release monitoring, honest version footer, pin package json
recipe: Pin APP.VERSION in the single constants module to exactly package.json's version.
Display it in Settings so the running build's identity is visible and auditable.
Never hardcode a version string at the point of display.
acceptance: APP.VERSION equals package.json version
the footer shows it and a test asserts the display
patterns.guardrail: Trust through honesty: monitoring and user support key off the real version; a drifted string is treated as a bug.

patterns.name: proof-of-delivery-probe
patterns.trigger: infra not live, publication not applied, smtp blocked, prove delivery, subscribe not delivered, exit code script probe, verify live
recipe: For infra claims that cannot be believed from config alone, write a scripted probe that exercises the REAL path.
Sign in with a real account, subscribe, perform a real mutation, and assert the event is DELIVERED.
Use distinct exit codes: 0 delivered, 1 config missing, 2 no delivery — so CI/operator can distinguish 'not run' from 'failed'.
acceptance: the probe exits 2 when the infra is genuinely not live (e.g. publication missing)
it never reports success on a merely SUBSCRIBED channel
patterns.guardrail: Evidence over narrative: a claim like 'realtime works' requires delivery proof, not an optimistic subscription status.

patterns.name: ci-collection-exclusion
patterns.trigger: vitest collects playwright, ci failed collection, exclude e2e glob, mixed test harnesses, runner include pattern
recipe: When a runner's default include glob pulls in another harness's specs (e.g. vitest collecting Playwright .spec.ts), exclude those paths in the runner's config.
Keep both suites independent: each runs under its own runner; never delete or weaken either suite's assertions.
acceptance: vitest collects zero Playwright specs
the Playwright suite still runs under its own runner and CI stays green
patterns.guardrail: Never weaken a test to pass a build: fix the collection boundary, not the assertions.
